cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tibia

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates distally with talus and fibula; proximally with femur and fibula.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Medial malleolus, tibial plafond, anterior border and interosseous border.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Medial malleolus lies medially; sharp anterior border faces forward.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Medial malleolus

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Distal tibia.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms the medial wall of the ankle mortise and articulates with the medial surface of the talus.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Gives attachment to the medial (deltoid) ligament of the ankle.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Fibula

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with tibia proximally and distally; lateral malleolus articulates with talus.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Head, neck, shaft and lateral malleolus.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Lateral malleolus projects more distally and posteriorly than the medial malleolus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lateral malleolus

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Distal fibula.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms the lateral wall of the ankle mortise and articulates with the lateral surface of the talus.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Gives attachment to lateral ankle ligaments and fibular retinacula.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Calcaneus

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with talus superiorly and cuboid anteriorly.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Calcaneal tuberosity, sustentaculum tali and fibular trochlea.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Achilles tendon inserts posteriorly; plantar fascia and several intrinsic foot muscles attach to the calcaneal tuberosity.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Forms the heel and transmits weight to the ground.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Talus

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with tibia, fibula, calcaneus and navicular.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Head, neck, body, trochlea and posterior process.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transfers body weight from tibia to the foot.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Has no muscular attachments and a vulnerable blood supply, making talar fractures prone to avascular necrosis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Navicular

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with talar head proximally and the three cuneiforms distally.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Navicular tuberosity on medial side.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Tibialis posterior inserts mainly onto the navicular tuberosity.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: 1st metatarsal

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates proximally with medial cuneiform and distally with proximal phalanx of hallux.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Base, shaft and head; head has grooves for sesamoid bones.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms the medial forefoot and contributes to the medial longitudinal arch.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: 5th metatarsal

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates proximally with cuboid and distally with proximal phalanx of little toe.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Prominent tuberosity at base.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms the lateral border of the forefoot.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tuberosity of 5th metatarsal

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Base of the 5th metatarsal.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Fibularis brevis inserts here; lateral band of plantar aponeurosis also attaches.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Avulsion fractures may occur with forceful inversion of the foot.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tibialis anterior

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Dorsiflexes ankle and inverts foot; supports medial longitudinal arch.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep fibular nerve (L4–L5).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lateral condyle and superior lateral tibia with interosseous membrane.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial cuneiform and base of 1st metatarsal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Extensor hallucis longus

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends hallux and dorsiflexes ankle.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep fibular nerve (L5).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Middle anterior fibula and interosseous membrane.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Dorsal base of distal phalanx of hallux.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Extensor digitorum longus

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends lateral four toes and dorsiflexes ankle; assists eversion.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep fibular nerve (L5–S1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lateral tibial condyle, anterior fibula and interosseous membrane.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Extensor expansions of lateral four toes.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Fibularis (peroneus) tertius

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Dorsiflexes ankle and assists eversion.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep fibular nerve (L5–S1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Inferior anterior fibula and interosseous membrane.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Dorsum of base of 5th metatarsal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Extensor digitorum brevis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Assists extension of toes 2–4.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep fibular nerve (L5–S1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Superolateral calcaneus.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Tendons to toes 2–4 joining extensor expansions.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Extensor hallucis brevis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends the hallux at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep fibular nerve (L5–S1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Superolateral calcaneus as medial part of extensor digitorum brevis complex.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Dorsal base of proximal phalanx of hallux.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Fibularis (peroneus) brevis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Everts foot and weakly plantarflexes ankle.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Superficial fibular nerve (L5–S2).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Inferior two-thirds of lateral fibula.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Tuberosity at base of 5th metatarsal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Fibularis (peroneus) longus

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Everts foot, weakly plantarflexes ankle and supports transverse/lateral arches.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Superficial fibular nerve (L5–S2).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Head and superior lateral fibula.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Base of 1st metatarsal and medial cuneiform on plantar surface.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Calcaneal (Achilles) tendon

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Formed mainly by gastrocnemius and soleus tendons, with variable plantaris contribution.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Posterior calcaneal tuberosity.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transmits triceps surae force for powerful plantarflexion.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Achilles rupture causes marked weakness of plantarflexion and an abnormal Thompson test.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor hallucis longus

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes hallux, plantarflexes ankle and supports medial longitudinal arch.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Tibial nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Inferior posterior fibula and interosseous membrane.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Base of distal phalanx of hallux.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor digitorum longus

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes lateral four toes, plantarflexes ankle and supports longitudinal arches.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Tibial nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Posterior tibia inferior to soleal line.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Bases of distal phalanges of toes 2–5.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor digitorum longus tendon

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes posterior to medial malleolus, enters sole and divides into four tendons for toes 2–5.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Bases of distal phalanges of toes 2–5.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transmits flexor digitorum longus force to flex the lateral four toes.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Receives insertion of quadratus plantae and gives origin to lumbricals in the sole.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Quadratus plantae

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Assists flexor digitorum longus by straightening its oblique pull on toes 2–5.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Lateral plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Medial and lateral plantar surfaces of calcaneus.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Posterolateral margin of flexor digitorum longus tendon.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tibialis posterior tendon

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes posterior to medial malleolus and deep to flexor retinaculum before entering medial foot.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Mainly navicular tuberosity, with expansions to cuneiforms, cuboid and bases of metatarsals 2–4.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transmits tibialis posterior force for inversion, plantarflexion and support of medial longitudinal arch.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Abductor hallucis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Abducts and flexes hallux; supports medial longitudinal arch.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Medial plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Medial calcaneal tubercle, flexor retinaculum and plantar aponeurosis.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial base of proximal phalanx of hallux.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor hallucis brevis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes hallux at the metatarsophalangeal joint and supports medial arch.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Medial plantar nerve, with possible lateral plantar contribution to lateral head (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Plantar cuboid and lateral cuneiform with tendon of tibialis posterior.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Both sides of base of proximal phalanx of hallux via sesamoids.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor digitorum brevis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes toes 2–5 at proximal interphalangeal joints.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Medial plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Medial calcaneal tubercle and plantar aponeurosis.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Sides of middle phalanges of toes 2–5.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor digiti minimi brevis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes the 5th toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Superficial branch of lateral plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Base of 5th metatarsal and sheath of fibularis longus tendon.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Base of proximal phalanx of 5th toe.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Abductor digiti minimi

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Abducts and flexes 5th toe; supports lateral longitudinal arch.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Lateral plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Calcaneal tuberosity and plantar aponeurosis.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral base of proximal phalanx of 5th toe.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lumbricals

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flex metatarsophalangeal joints and extend interphalangeal joints of toes 2–5.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: 1st lumbrical: medial plantar nerve; 2nd–4th: lateral plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Tendons of flexor digitorum longus.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial sides of extensor expansions of toes 2–5.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Adductor hallucis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Adducts hallux and supports transverse arch of foot.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep branch of lateral plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral side of base of proximal phalanx of hallux.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Oblique head of adductor hallucis
cards.label: 31a

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Bases of metatarsals 2–4 and sheath of fibularis longus tendon.
cards.label: 31a

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Adducts hallux and contributes to transverse arch support.
cards.label: 31a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Transverse head of adductor hallucis
cards.label: 31b

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Plantar ligaments of metatarsophalangeal joints 3–5 and deep transverse metatarsal ligament.
cards.label: 31b

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Adducts hallux and helps maintain transverse arch.
cards.label: 31b

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Plantar interosseus

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Adducts toes 3–5 toward the 2nd toe; flexes MTP joints and extends IP joints.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Lateral plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Medial sides of metatarsals 3–5.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial bases of proximal phalanges and extensor expansions of toes 3–5.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Dorsal interosseus

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Abducts toes 2–4 from the axis of the 2nd toe; flexes MTP joints and extends IP joints.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Lateral plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Adjacent sides of metatarsals 1–5.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: 1st inserts medially on 2nd toe; others insert laterally on toes 2–4.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Inferior extensor retinaculum

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Y-shaped thickening of deep fascia attached laterally to calcaneus and medially toward medial malleolus/plantar aponeurosis region.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Holds anterior compartment extensor tendons close to the ankle and prevents bowstringing.

cards.question: Contents
cards.answer: Related to tendons of tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, extensor digitorum longus and fibularis tertius, with anterior tibial/dorsalis pedis vessels and deep fibular nerve.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor retinaculum of the foot

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends from medial malleolus to medial calcaneus.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Holds flexor tendons and neurovascular structures behind the medial malleolus.

cards.question: Contents
cards.answer: From anterior to posterior: tibialis posterior, flexor digitorum longus, posterior tibial vessels, tibial nerve, flexor hallucis longus.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Compression of tibial nerve deep to the retinaculum causes tarsal tunnel syndrome.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superior fibular (peroneal) retinaculum

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends from lateral malleolus to lateral calcaneus.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Holds fibularis longus and brevis tendons behind the lateral malleolus.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies superficial to the fibular tendons posterior to the lateral malleolus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Inferior fibular (peroneal) retinaculum

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Attaches to lateral calcaneus and blends anteriorly with the inferior extensor retinaculum.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Secures fibularis longus and brevis tendons against lateral calcaneus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Medial (deltoid) ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Broad ligament from medial malleolus to talus, calcaneus and navicular.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Includes tibionavicular, tibiocalcaneal, anterior tibiotalar and posterior tibiotalar components.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Stabilises medial ankle and strongly resists excessive eversion.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Anterior inferior tibiofibular ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Connects distal anterior tibia to distal fibula.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Stabilises the distal tibiofibular syndesmosis and ankle mortise.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Commonly injured in a high ankle sprain.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Posterior tibiofibular ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Connects posterior distal tibia to posterior distal fibula.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Reinforces the posterior distal tibiofibular syndesmosis and stabilises the ankle mortise.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Anterior tibial artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal branch of popliteal artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes through proximal interosseous membrane into anterior leg and descends with deep fibular nerve.

cards.question: Termination
cards.answer: Continues as dorsalis pedis artery distal to the ankle.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Anterior compartment of leg and dorsum of foot through its continuation.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Deep fibular (peroneal) nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: L4–S1, terminal branch of common fibular nerve.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends in anterior leg with anterior tibial artery and enters dorsum of foot deep to extensor retinacula.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies anterior compartment muscles and extensor digitorum brevis/extensor hallucis brevis.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Sensation to first dorsal web space.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes weakness of dorsiflexion and toe extension if injured proximally, with sensory loss in the first dorsal web space.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Medial dorsal cutaneous nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Branch of superficial fibular nerve.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes onto dorsum of foot and divides into dorsal digital branches.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Supplies much of medial dorsum of foot and dorsal aspects of adjacent toes, excluding key deep fibular/saphenous territories.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes numbness or paraesthesia over its cutaneous territory on the medial dorsum of the foot without motor weakness.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Branch of superficial fibular nerve.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs over dorsolateral foot and divides into dorsal digital branches.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Supplies central/lateral dorsum of foot and adjacent dorsal toe surfaces.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes numbness or paraesthesia over the central to lateral dorsum of the foot without motor weakness.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lateral dorsal cutaneous nerve (branch of sural nerve)

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Continuation/terminal branch of sural nerve.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes behind lateral malleolus onto lateral dorsum of foot.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Supplies lateral side of foot and lateral aspect of 5th toe.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes sensory loss or paraesthesia along the lateral foot and lateral aspect of the 5th toe.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lateral calcaneal branches of sural nerve

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Cutaneous branches of the sural nerve.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Supply skin over lateral heel.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes numbness or altered sensation over the lateral heel.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Arise near the lateral ankle/heel region.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Dorsalis pedis artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Continuation of anterior tibial artery distal to ankle.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs on dorsum of foot lateral to extensor hallucis longus tendon toward first intermetatarsal space.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Gives lateral tarsal, arcuate, dorsal metatarsal and deep plantar branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Dorsum of foot and contributes to plantar arch.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Deep plantar artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal deep plantar branch of dorsalis pedis artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes through first intermetatarsal space into sole.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Joins lateral plantar artery to complete the deep plantar arch.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Dorsal metatarsal arteries

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Arise mainly from arcuate artery and dorsalis pedis system.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Run distally in dorsal intermetatarsal spaces.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Dorsum of toes and adjacent foot through dorsal digital branches.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lateral calcaneal branches of fibular artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Branches derived from the fibular (peroneal) artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Reach the lateral calcaneal/heel region.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Lateral heel and adjacent tissues.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ramus communicans (communicating branch)

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Provides an anastomotic communication between distal posterior tibial and fibular arterial territories.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Located in the distal posterior leg/ankle vascular network.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Posterior tibial artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal branch of popliteal artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends in deep posterior leg and passes behind medial malleolus beneath flexor retinaculum.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Gives fibular artery, calcaneal branches and terminates as medial and lateral plantar arteries.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Posterior leg and plantar foot through its branches.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Medial calcaneal branches of posterior tibial artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Branches of posterior tibial artery near the ankle.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Medial heel and calcaneal region.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Medial plantar artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Smaller terminal branch of posterior tibial artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs anteriorly along medial sole with medial plantar nerve.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Medial sole and hallux region.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lateral plantar artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Larger terminal branch of posterior tibial artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs obliquely across sole then curves medially to form most of the deep plantar arch.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Lateral sole and much of plantar forefoot.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Deep plantar arch

cards.question: Formation
cards.answer: Formed mainly by lateral plantar artery and completed medially by deep plantar branch of dorsalis pedis.

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Deep in sole across bases of metatarsals.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Gives plantar metatarsal arteries and perforating branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Deep plantar forefoot and toes through branches.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Plantar metatarsal artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Branches of the deep plantar arch.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Run distally in plantar intermetatarsal spaces.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Divide into plantar digital arteries supplying toes.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tibial nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: L4–S3, terminal branch of sciatic nerve.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends in posterior leg, passes behind medial malleolus beneath flexor retinaculum and divides into medial/lateral plantar nerves.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies posterior leg and, through plantar branches, most intrinsic muscles of sole.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Supplies heel and sole via calcaneal and plantar branches.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Proximal injury causes weak plantarflexion, toe flexion and inversion with sensory loss over the sole; compression at the tarsal tunnel mainly causes plantar pain/paraesthesia and intrinsic foot weakness.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Medial plantar nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Terminal branch of tibial nerve, mainly L4–L5.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs anteriorly in medial sole with medial plantar artery.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis, flexor hallucis brevis and first lumbrical.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Supplies medial sole and plantar surfaces of medial 3½ toes.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes sensory disturbance over the medial sole and medial 3½ toes with weakness of muscles such as abductor hallucis; entrapment may cause 'jogger's foot'.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lateral plantar nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Terminal branch of tibial nerve, mainly S1–S2.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs obliquely across sole with lateral plantar artery and divides into superficial/deep branches.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies most intrinsic muscles of sole not supplied by medial plantar nerve.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Supplies lateral sole and plantar surfaces of lateral 1½ toes.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Causes weakness of most intrinsic foot muscles with sensory loss or paraesthesia over the lateral sole and lateral 1½ toes.
